desc: Brute-force (BFS over configs, small N) the exact reachability in ≤k operations; build harness to test candidate feasibility predicates (notes show monotone assignment + |disp|≤k is NOT sufficient: S_A={1,3,5}→S_B={1,3,4} with k=1 is a counterexample).

Execute the harness (or hand-compute the decisive case: all 25 two-step sequences from {1,3,5} → is {1,3,4} reachable at k=2?) and record outputs (a)–(d); determine whether the obstruction is k=1-only or extends to k≥2 via slack-1 pieces.

Based on the discovered characterization, design an efficient check(k) (or closed form) and prove it; handle the "stayer/wiggle" subtlety (pieces with slack < 2 have forced paths; simultaneous single-target constraint per step).
Determine impossibility criteria (e.g., spread of S_B > spread of S_A, or no assignment for any k ≤ N) and how they fall out of the characterization.
Implement the full algorithm (likely binary search on k with O(M) check, or direct greedy for min k) with fast I/O for T up to 2e5, sum N ≤ 1e6.
Validate the implementation against the brute force on random small cases and against the three provided samples (expected 3, -1, 5).
